title: Rate limits & org/project keys demo with Medisys Health
next_steps: Send rate-limit config examples and pricing tiers
Schedule pilot onboarding call for week of Dec 1
Provide sample org/project key rollout plan and migration notes
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (CTO, Medisys), Andre Gomes (Platform), Priya Rao (Security)

Summary: Quick demo of Redwood Console and API focusing on rate limits, org/project keys, quotas, and multi-tenant controls. Covered hosted vs dedicated routing, per-project quotas, token-based project keys, and audit logging. Customer asked about SSO, data residency, and how we enforce guardrails for noisy tenants. Agreed next steps to send docs and schedule pilot onboarding.

[00:00] Ethan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ethan Park from Redwood Inference. Sofia's on from our engineering team, she'll run the deep config bits.
[00:12] Laura: Hey Ethan, hi Sofia, thanks. We have Andre and Priya on. We're primarily interested in multi-tenant rate limiting and isolation — we run in-prod gen features and need soft and hard quotas.
[00:25] Sofia: Great. Quick agenda: demo Console rate-limit UI, show API keys -> org/project model, show Optimize suggestions for batching and quant profiles, then Q&A.
[00:38] Andre: Cool. A few constraints up front: we need per-tenant quotas, ability to throttle by route, and audit logs for compliance. We also need to consider on-prem options later.
[00:50] Sofia: Understood. We'll show Hosted API controls first — these map to org and project keys, then how Dedicated / Private differ.

[02:05] Sofia: (screen share) This is the Redwood Console. On the left is Organizations, you can see our sample org: "MediSys-POC". Clicking into Projects shows project-level keys. Note the key model: org-level admin keys, project-level client keys.
[02:25] Laura: Is that the same as api token scoping? We want one key per product and then rotate per customer tenant.
[02:34] Ethan: Yes, exactly. Project keys are intended to be embedded in apps; org keys are admin only. We recommend per-customer project keys for multi-tenant setups.
[02:46] Andre: How does rate limiting apply? Can we set both default global limits and per-project overrides?
[02:55] Sofia: Yep. Here in the Rate Limits tab you can see global policy and then project overrides. Defaults are token-per-minute and token-per-day; you can add route-specific rules (e.g., embeddings vs. completion).
[03:15] Sofia: (small typo in UI reading) we also have spike protection — circuit-breaker style — for noisy tenants, which will shed traffic to prevent tail latency spikes.
[03:30] Priya: For compliance, do you log user-level request metadata? We need audit trails that show which project key invoked what model and the payload hash, without storing PII.
[03:45] Sofia: Audit logs capture request id, project key id, model used, token counts, latency, and optionally request metadata flags. We redact user PII by default but can retain hashes for debugging.

[05:10] Ethan: Quick note on hosted vs dedicated: hosted gives you rate-limit and quota controls in Console; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and the same policy surface but isolated infra. Private deployments include the control plane you manage.
[05:28] Andre: If we go Dedicated, will the org/project keys still be managed in your control plane or ours?
[05:36] Sofia: For Dedicated we can host the control plane or run a customer-managed control plane — we have both patterns. Keys can be stored in your KMS if you prefer.

[07:00] Sofia: Now demoing API. Example curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer prj_live_xxx" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions. Server responds with quota headers: X-Redwood-RateLimit-Limit, X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset.
[07:20] Andre: Nice, headers are helpful. Can those be customized per route? For example, different bucket for embeddings.
[07:28] Sofia: Yes, you can define buckets by route or by model family. In the Console you can attach a bucket to a project or a route.
[07:38] Laura: Any soft-limit alerts? We want to be notified before a tenant hits a hard cap.
[07:44] Ethan: You can configure thresholds and alerting to Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook. Also the Console shows projected burn based on recent rate.

[09:05] Sofia: (typing) showing Rate Limit policy editor. Here's a policy: default 1M tokens/day per org, projects inherit, but you can set Project A to 100k/day. Also per-minute peak 200 tokens/sec.
[09:25] Andre: That per-minute seems low for our embedding bursts. Can we set burst window and refill rate?
[09:33] Sofia: Yes — we support burst tokens and refill interval. There's also continuous batching which helps absorb short bursts without hitting per-request limits.

[11:10] Priya: On security: we need SSO for admin console, RBAC for who can create keys, and policy-based access for teams.
[11:22] Ethan: We support SAML SSO, SCIM user provisioning, and RBAC roles: Org Admin, Project Admin, Viewer, etc. We also surface key creation events in audit logs.
[11:35] Priya: Do you integrate with our KMS? We want keys wrapped by our HSM.
[11:41] Sofia: Yes, for Private and Dedicated you can use customer-managed KMS/HSM. For hosted, we manage keys but can offer a bring-your-own-KMS integration for enterprise contracts.

[13:00] Sofia: Switching to Optimize briefly — Optimize will analyze call patterns and recommend batching and quantization profiles to reduce token cost. For multi-tenant workloads it can suggest per-project quant profiles to keep latency within SLOs.
[13:22] Laura: Is Optimize automated or advisory? We don't want it to change production config without review.
[13:30] Sofia: It's advisory by default. You can opt in to automated reconfiguration, but typical customers review suggestions first.

[15:05] Andre: How do you handle fallback when a model is unavailable? We need graceful degradation to cheaper/older model to keep user experience.
[15:16] Ethan: We have route policies for model fallback — automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to a degraded service tier. You can define priorities and percentage rollouts.

[17:50] Sofia: Demo: creating a new project key and attaching a quota. (minor transcription glitch) here I create key prj_demo_456, set daily token limit to 150k, set burst to 10k, and attach route rule: embeddings -> separate bucket.
[18:10] Andre: If a tenant exceeds the rate, is traffic rejected or queued?
[18:16] Sofia: By default hard-limit rejects with 429. You can configure soft-limits to queue or to route to cached responses or lowered-quality model.

[19:50] Laura: We have a legal requirement around data residency for EU customers, can we restrict project keys to certain regions?
[20:02] Ethan: Yes, routing policies can pin requests by project to region and failover to another region if you allow it. For Private deployments you control physical region entirely.

[22:30] Priya: On observability, what do your dashboards show? We need token usage per project, latency percentiles, and per-key error rates.
[22:45] Sofia: Console dashboards include per-project token counts, per-route latency p50/p95/p99, error counts by status code, and audit logs. We also provide CSV/SQL export and metrics via Prometheus.

[24:12] Andre: Any real-world limits customers hit? e.g., noisy tenant patterns?
[24:20] Sofia: A common pattern: a single tenant spikes embeddings and causes token burn. Spike protection + per-project burst windows addresses that. We also recommend per-tenant keys and client-side rate limiting as defense-in-depth.

[26:00] Laura: Pricing question: do you charge per-token before or after retries and queuing?
[26:08] Ethan: We bill per successfully processed token. Retries that result in successful tokens counted; failed attempts are not billed. If we do caching/hits, cached responses don't count full model tokens. We'll send detailed pricing tiers.

[28:30] Sofia: Walkthrough of REST API logs. You can see header X-Redwood-Project: prj_demo_456 and then X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 42. The API also returns upcoming-model suggestion header when Optimize thinks a cheaper model is acceptable.
[29:12] Andre: That header sounds useful. Is Optimize model suggestion based on quality thresholds?
[29:20] Sofia: Yes, it's based on eval thresholds you configure — you set acceptable drop in ROUGE/embedding-sim threshold and Optimize will only suggest models within that band.

[31:00] Priya: For audit we need tamper-evident logs. Do you support log signing or append-only storage?
[31:08] Ethan: We support write-once S3 buckets with server-side encryption and can integrate with your SIEM. For higher assurance, we can provide signed digest exports on request.

[33:40] Sofia: (typo) showing canary policies — you can do percent rollouts per project. Also automatic fallback if latency exceeds threshold for X minutes.
[34:00] Laura: Good, can we limit who can create canary rollouts?
[34:06] Ethan: RBAC controls that, only Org Admins and Release Managers roles by policy.

[36:20] Andre: How do we migrate existing API keys? We have a monolithic key scheme across apps.
[36:28] Sofia: We recommend phased migration: create project keys, proxy traffic, validate quotas, then rotate old keys. We have scripts and a migration playbook we'll share.

[38:50] Laura: Any gotchas with Dedicated when it comes to quotas? I assume Dedicated gives predictable throughput but we still need token-level quotas.
[38:59] Sofia: Correct — Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity but quotas and rate-limits are enforced at the control plane level which can be hosted or customer-managed. If you host control plane, you version policies with our CLI.

[40:10] Priya: We want to run a short pilot — can you provide a sample rate-limit policy and an evaluation notebook?
[40:18] Ethan: Yes, we'll send a starter policy, a benchmarking checklist, and an evaluation notebook that uses your sample prompts.

[42:00] (short side conversation about calendar availability)

[44:05] Recap (Ethan): - Send rate-limit config examples and pricing - Share SOC2 + security whitepaper - Schedule pilot onboarding for week of Dec 1 - Provide migration playbook and key rotation scripts
[44:20] Laura: That sounds good. One more ask: can you send an example of a per-tenant SLA and what happens on breach?
[44:29] Ethan: We'll include a sample SLA doc and failure modes.

[45:10] Sofia: Anything else on the technical side?
[45:15] Andre: No, that's it. We'll review docs and get back to schedule.
[45:22] Priya: We'll also loop in legal for the residency notes.
[45:30] Ethan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and a suggested pilot timeline.
[45:36] Laura: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription has minor errors (some product names mis-heard) — e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicatede'. References to headers and API paths are illustrative.
